input: An amine absorption unit treating gas from a cement kiln has been tested at pilot scale, and over the course of a 60-day pilot run at 14 t of carbon dioxide per day it captured no less than 91% of the carbon dioxide present in the treated gas. The capture figure represents the share of the carbon dioxide entering with the treated gas that the solvent took up across the run as a whole. In terms of energy, the steam demand was 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, and since steam is the energy input that regeneration of the solvent consumes, this figure effectively prices the capture in energy terms. Solvent loss, meanwhile, was 1.8 kg per tonne captured, which is a consumable cost that runs alongside the steam. Taken together, the three figures describe the unit as tested: the capture rate, the energy taken to hold it, and the solvent consumed in holding it. It is important to note, however, that every figure is a 60-day figure. Beyond 60 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested, and capture, steam demand and solvent loss have not been established for a longer campaign.
